Crazy Tube Circuits browse by type volume/amplification amplification treble booster browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive fuzz browse by type pitch/octave octaver octave fuzz browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive overdrive browse by enclosure pedal events 2026 NAMM 2026 Crazy Tube Circuits Triptychon - Octave Fuzz / Drive / Treble Boost Published on January 23, 2026 Crazy Tube Circuits fuzz octave fuzz overdrive treble boost pedal NAMM 2026 NAMM 2026 NAMM 2026 Information The Crazy Tube Circuits Triptychon is a fully analog multi-effect guitar pedal that combines a multi-voice fuzz circuit, a selectable upper octave or boost stage, and an assignable drive section within a single enclosure. The design follows a three-part concept intended to recreate the signal chain interaction found in classic recordings, where fuzz, octave effects, or treble boosters were driven into already overdriven amplifiers. Each section operates independently or in combination, allowing flexible routing and gain staging that reflects both vintage and modern pedalboard configurations. The central fuzz section forms the core of the circuit and features four selectable voices inspired by Dallas Arbiter Fuzz Face, Vox Tone Bender, Sola Sound Tone Bender Mk1.5, and Tone Bender MkII designs. It uses a custom configuration of metal-can silicon transistors engineered to replicate the dynamic response, cleanup behavior, and touch sensitivity associated with germanium-based fuzz circuits, while maintaining consistent performance across varying environmental conditions. The right-side section functions as either an upper octave fuzz or a boost circuit. In octave mode, it generates an upper octave effect with two selectable voicings, ranging from cleaner, more defined responses to louder and more harmonically rich textures inspired by classic octave fuzz designs. In boost mode, the circuit operates as a treble or mid-focused booster, with selectable voicings that shift between a traditional bright emphasis and a fuller midrange response. This section shares the same silicon transistor approach as the fuzz circuit to maintain consistent interaction characteristics.
